cards.text: Malaysian rules bar bulk exports of blended palm oil unless every shipping paper states the mix. A complaint says one Port Klang cargo's papers did not.
cards.sub: The complaint, about the tanker MT Eunice on 30 Sep, is unproven. MPOB acknowledged it in writing on 22 Oct and has said nothing in public since.
sources: MPOB (Quality) Regulations 2005, P.U.(A) 518/2005, reg. 12(1) and 12(3)(a)-(c) [brief S1]
The Sun 17 Nov 2026 and MPOB Palm News republication [S16a, S7c]; Utusan Malaysia 17 Nov 2026 ('merekodkan aduan berkenaan') [S17a]; Oriental Daily [S17b]
No MPOB, ministry, Olam or Mewah public statement found, 22 Oct to 18 Nov 2026 (brief KEY STATISTICS row 22)

cards.h: Port agent Maritime Network alleges Indonesian palm oil was mixed aboard MT Eunice with about 5,000 tonnes of Malaysian crude palm olein, then declared as crude palm olein for Egypt.
cards.s: The agent signed the bills of lading and now seeks an indemnity from trader Olam, which has made no public statement. Its own letter says the mix still needs documentary verification.
cards.d: Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, the port agent appointed by the vessel's owner, alleges that on 30 Sep 2026 Indonesian refined palm product was mixed aboard MT Eunice at Port Klang with 4,999.715 tonnes of Malaysian crude palm olein, that the bill of lading was changed so the whole cargo was declared as crude palm olein, and that the shipper named was a Malaysian company; the cargo sailed for Adabiya, Egypt. Its CEO lodged a complaint with MPOB on 19 Oct. Its lawyers' letter of demand to Olam Global Agri Pte Ltd (29 Oct) says Maritime Network 'signed the bills of lading on behalf of the vessel's master', disputes Olam's alleged assertion that it knew of and consented to the arrangements, seeks an indemnity, and 'acknowledged that the precise nature and extent of any commingling still needed documentary verification' (all as reported by Malay Mail). The Indonesian outward manifest is described as listing RBD palm oil, RBD palm stearin and RBD palm kernel oil; press reports say RBD palm olein. No source says any document declared Malaysian origin or that a certificate of origin was issued. Tonnages conflict: the letter gives about 35,432 t loaded at Dumai; the complainant later estimated about 15,000 t in total. Only the Port Klang parcel figure is used. Mewah Oils Sdn Bhd is named only as seller of the Malaysian parcel; no wrongdoing is alleged against it.
sources: Malay Mail 5 Nov 2026, report of the 29 Oct letter of demand (Jaya Prem Chambers) [S15]
The Sun 17 Nov 2026 [S16a]; Utusan Malaysia 17 Nov 2026 (about 15,000 t estimate) [S17a]; Oriental Daily [S17b]

cards.h: Malaysia imported 764,863 tonnes of palm oil in 2025, three times the 253,485 tonnes it imported in 2024. It exported 15.27 million tonnes.
cards.s: One industry research note ties the rise mainly to local oleochemical plants. MPOB publishes import totals but no source we found shows how much imported oil is blended and shipped out again.
cards.d: MPOB's 2025 overview gives palm oil imports of 764,863 t in 2025 against 253,485 t in 2024 ('3-folds'), with exports of 15,272,823 t in 2025; origin of imports is not broken out in the table. MBSB Research, summarising MPOB's January 2026 outlook seminar, attributed the rise 'terutama untuk penggunaan kilang oleokimia tempatan' (mainly for local oleochemical plants). Market talk reported by The Edge (4 Nov 2026) describes an alleged 'cocktail' of imported and local oil with 'blending ratios of 75:25 or 80:20 reportedly circulating'; that is unverified and not used on the card. Monthly imports fell to 26,207 t of processed palm oil in October 2026, with crude palm oil imports at zero. Exports to the EU were 1.03 Mt (6.8%) in 2025; the EU Deforestation Regulation applies to EU-bound product from 30 Dec 2026; the Egypt cargo is outside it.
sources: MPOB, Overview of the Malaysian Oil Palm Industry 2025, summary table (exports, imports) [S6]
MBSB Research via Utusan, 19 Jan 2026 [S22c]; The Edge 4 Nov 2026 [S18]; Bernama 10 Nov 2026 (October data) [S22a]
Regulation (EU) 2025/2650, new Art. 38(2) [S9]; Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 Art. 2(16), (37), Art. 3 [S8]

cards.h: MPOB's Act bars disclosure of what its officers gather, and lets the Director-General settle an untrue export declaration by compound. Prosecution is then barred.
cards.s: Nothing in the Act requires MPOB to publish outcomes. A blending offence under reg. 12 cannot be compounded, so proving one would mean a charge, with the Public Prosecutor's consent.
cards.d: Malaysian Palm Oil Board Act 1998 (Act 582): s. 66(1) 'Except for the purposes of this Act, no person who has access to any record ... information, document or other material obtained under this Act shall disclose such ... to any other person'; s. 67 untrue, inaccurate or misleading declarations (up to RM100,000, two years, or both); s. 71 the Director-General may compound a prescribed offence for up to 50% of the maximum fine before prosecution, after which 'no prosecution shall thereafter be instituted'; s. 72(1) prosecution needs the Public Prosecutor's written consent. The MPOB (Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2005 schedule lists Act s. 67 and several Licensing Regulations offences, and no Quality Regulations offence, so reg. 12 (blending) is not compoundable on that schedule. No duty to publish investigation or compound outcomes was found in the Act. The same Act gives MPOB the objective 'to promote and develop the oil palm industry' (s. 3(2)(a)) and the function 'to regulate ... export and import of oil palm products' (s. 4(d)). Powers at the port: exporters file Form MPOB Q1 at least two days before loading (Quality reg. 4); officers 'may take samples in any manner as he deems fit' where product is suspected blended (reg. 9(3)); customs officers are authorised officers (s. 2). Later amendments to the compounding schedule not found (brief GAP 8).
sources: Malaysian Palm Oil Board Act 1998 (Act 582): ss. 2, 3(2)(a), 4(d), 66, 67, 71, 72 [S3a]
MPOB (Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2005, P.U.(A) 519/2005, reg. 2 and Schedule [S2c]

cards.text: MPOB can sample a suspect cargo, compound a false declaration and close the file. Its Act lets it do all three without a public word.
sources: Quality reg. 9(3) [S1]; Act 582 ss. 66, 71 [S3a]; Compounding Regulations 2005 Schedule [S2c]

cards.text: Picture a food inspector who can test the kitchen and fine the cook on the spot, but never has to post the result on the door.
sources: Rests on the same provisions: sampling reg. 9(3) [S1]; compounding s. 71 and secrecy s. 66 [S3a]

cards.text: Blending palm oil is legal when the papers say so. Whether this cargo's papers did is a question only MPOB can answer, and nothing in its Act requires an answer.
sources: Quality reg. 12(3) [S1]; Act 582 s. 66, no publication duty found [S3a]

headline_suggestion: Palm oil blend complaint at Port Klang: MPOB acknowledged it on 22 Oct, has said nothing since
context_suggestion: Malaysia's 2005 palm oil quality rules allow bulk blends only when the contract and every shipping paper state the mix. A port agent's complaint about a 30 Sep cargo bound for Egypt sits with MPOB.
sources: MPOB (Quality) Regulations 2005 (P.U.(A) 518/2005); MPOB (Licensing) Regulations 2005 (P.U.(A) 516/2005); MPOB (Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2005 (P.U.(A) 519/2005); Malaysian Palm Oil Board Act 1998 (Act 582); MPOB Overview of the Malaysian Oil Palm Industry 2025; Regulation (EU) 2023/1115; Regulation (EU) 2025/2650; Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1093; Malay Mail 5 Nov 2026 (letter of demand); The Sun 17 Nov 2026; Utusan Malaysia 17 Nov 2026; Oriental Daily 17 Nov 2026; The Edge 4 Nov 2026; Bernama 10 Nov 2026; MBSB Research via Utusan 19 Jan 2026
confidence: Medium. HIGH on the law (Act 582, Quality, Licensing and Compounding Regulations opened in gazetted text) and on MPOB national data and EU texts. LOW on the incident: every fact about the cargo comes from the complainant, a party seeking an indemnity, or reporting of its documents; the counterparty has made no public statement; tonnages conflict; MPOB's 22 Oct letter is unpublished and described differently by The Sun ('confirmed' an investigation) and Utusan ('recorded' the complaint). The cards therefore attribute every case fact and use 'acknowledged in writing'.
needs_verification: MPOB's 22 Oct letter: whether it confirms an investigation or only records the complaint. Cards say 'acknowledged it in writing'; attribute 'confirmed an investigation' to The Sun if used anywhere.

Whether reg. 12 reaches mixing aboard a ship after the Malaysian parcel is deemed exported on loading (Quality reg. 16, Licensing reg. 47) and the Indonesian cargo is in transit (Customs Act s. 2). The hook says the rules 'bar bulk exports of blended palm oil unless every shipping paper states the mix', which is reg. 12's text; whether it applies to this transfer is open.
Compounding schedule: confirm no later amendment to P.U.(A) 519/2005 adds Quality Regulations offences; fact 3's 'cannot be compounded' depends on it.
Imports 764,863 t (2025) vs 253,485 t (2024) from MPOB's 2025 overview table; confirm the units and that both figures are palm oil (not palm kernel oil).
Any public statement by MPOB, the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities, Customs, Olam Global Agri or Mewah Oils at publication; the hook's 'has said nothing in public since' must be re-checked.
Whether any certificate of origin was issued for the cargo, and by whom (MITI-authorised chamber); no card claims a Malaysian-origin declaration.
source_notes: (1) MPOB letter of 22 Oct: The Sun and The Vibes say it 'confirmed' an investigation; Utusan says it recorded the complaint and did not confirm the claims; Oriental Daily says it confirmed formal recording. The letter is unpublished; cards use 'acknowledged in writing'. (2) Tonnage: letter of demand ~35,432 t at Dumai + 4,999.715 t at Port Klang; complainant's later estimate ~15,000 t total. Only the Port Klang parcel is used ('about 5,000 tonnes'); no Malaysian share is computed. (3) Indonesian product: press says RBD palm olein; the manifest, per the letter, lists RBD palm oil, stearin and palm kernel oil; card says 'Indonesian palm oil'. (4) Consent dispute direction: Olam allegedly asserted Maritime Network knew and consented; Maritime Network disputes it. (5) The working thesis said papers were changed to declare 'Malaysian' crude palm olein; sources say crude palm olein with a Malaysian shipper; no origin declaration is reported. (6) Import rise: MBSB ties it mainly to oleochemical plants; market talk of a re-export 'cocktail' is unverified and kept off cards.
guardrails_applied: Every case fact attributed to the complainant; the complainant's commercial interest (indemnity, signed the bills of lading) stated on fact 1.
No card says blending is illegal: hook and view state reg. 12's conditional rule.
No card says the cargo was declared 'Malaysian'; no certificate of origin claimed.
Mewah Oils not named on cards; Olam named only as the party from which an indemnity is sought, with 'no public statement'.
EUDR kept to fact 2's detail as context; the cards do not say EUDR applies to the Egypt cargo.
Fact 3 states the counterweight: reg. 12 is not compoundable, so a proven blending offence would mean a charge.
No nationality framing of Indonesian oil as inferior; the issue is declaration.
Avoids issue 2017's 'Malaysian label is a national asset' reframe and its 'provenance' elevated word.
